fullPassage: A professor had students craft poetry-generating programs. The children would feed the program verbs, adjectives, and nouns, and the computer would combine them into lines of poetry: "MAD WOLF HATES BECAUSE INSANE WOLF SKIPS" or "UGLY MAN LOVES BECAUSE UGLY DOG HATES." The process of trying to get the program to work lent students startling insights into language. Jenny, a thirteen-year-old girl who had previously earned only mediocre grades, came in one day and announced, "Now I know why we have nouns and verbs." She'd been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them. But as Jenny struggled to get the program to work, she realized she had to classify words into categories—all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another—or else the sentences the computer spat out wouldn't make sense. Grammar suddenly became deeply meaningful. This produced another effect: Jenny began getting A's in her language classes.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 명사 meaning → 형용사 meaningful: became의 보어가 되는 형용사 자리
det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'became deeply __________'에서 became(~이 되었다)의 보어이면서 부사 deeply의 꾸밈을 받는 형용사 자리예요. 명사 meaning(의미)을 형용사 meaningful(의미 있는)로 바꿔 'deeply meaningful(깊이 의미 있는)'이 됩니다.

questions.passage: A professor had students craft poetry-generating programs. The children would feed the program verbs, adjectives, and nouns, and the computer would combine them into lines of poetry: "MAD WOLF HATES BECAUSE INSANE WOLF SKIPS" or "UGLY MAN LOVES BECAUSE UGLY DOG HATES." The process of trying to get the program to work lent students startling __________. Jenny, a thirteen-year-old girl who had previously earned only mediocre grades, came in one day and announced, "Now I know why we have nouns and verbs." She'd been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them. But as Jenny struggled to get the program to work, she realized she had to classify words into categories—all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another—or else the sentences the computer spat out wouldn't make sense. Grammar suddenly became deeply meaningful. This produced another effect: Jenny began getting A's in her language classes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 = insights into language(언어에 대한 통찰): 프로그램 작동 시도가 학생에게 준 것
det.analysis:
❌ ① rewards for winning(승리의 보상): 본문과 무관해요.
✅ ② insights into language(언어에 대한 통찰): 프로그램을 작동시키려는 과정이 학생들에게 언어에 대한 놀라운 통찰을 주었다는 흐름이라 적절해요. ←정답
❌ ③ breaks from study(공부에서의 휴식): 본문에 없어요.
❌ ④ copies of poems(시의 복사본): 무관해요.
det.tip: lent students startling ___ → insights into language

The process of trying to get the program to work lent students startling insights into language. Jenny, a thirteen-year-old girl who had previously earned only mediocre grades, came in one day and announced, "Now I know why we have nouns and verbs." She'd been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them. But as Jenny struggled to get the program to work, she realized she had to __________—all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another—or else the sentences the computer spat out wouldn't make sense. questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸 = classify words into categories(단어를 범주로 분류하다): Jenny가 해야 한다고 깨달은 일
det.analysis:
❌ ① memorize the whole poem(시 전체를 암기하다): 본문과 무관해요.
❌ ② delete all the verbs(모든 동사를 삭제하다): 문맥과 어긋나요.
✅ ③ classify words into categories(단어를 범주로 분류하다): 동사는 한 통에, 명사는 다른 통에 넣어야 문장이 말이 된다는 흐름이라 적절해요. ←정답
❌ ④ ignore the grammar rules(문법 규칙을 무시하다): 문법이 의미 있게 되었다는 흐름과 반대예요.
det.tip: all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another → classify words into categories
